WoW: Forever

Fury Warrior

Dual-wield rage dump, except that the spec's own gimmick is unavailable the whole time you level towards it: you cannot dual-wield until 20.

WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated October 8, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70245 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Fury build has been tested. Talent tiers unlock at 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and the capstone at 40. No source has posted a level 30 build either. The cap only reached 30 on October 1, and none of the three has published one since. The level 30 line below therefore extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs; it is not a build any guide has recommended. Blizzard's own caveat: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes." The crit-Rage bonus shows what that means in practice. It has already moved from 75% to 100% inside the beta, so treat the number as tuning in progress.

Blizzard's October 2 Fury pass has not reached the game yet. The newest build there is, 1.60.1.70245 of October 6, does not have it. Furious Precision, Lingering Rage and Gore Drinker are not in the tree, so you cannot select them and you cannot spend a point in them. Boundless RageBoundless RageTalentCastInstantIncreases your maximum Rage by 30. and Improved CleaveImproved CleaveTalentCastInstantReduces the Rage cost of your Cleave ability by 3. are both still sitting there with their old tooltips, though Blizzard's post says it deleted them. Booming VoiceBooming VoiceTalentCastInstantIncreases the radius of your Battle Shout and Demoralizing Shout abilities by 50%., Raging BlowsRaging BlowsTalentCastInstantCauses your Whirlwind to also strike with your Off Hand weapon, and reduces the Rage cost of your Cleave ability by 2., Blood CrazeBlood CrazeTalentCastInstantRegenerates 3% of your total Health over 6 sec after being the victim of a critical strike, dealing damage with Bloodthirst, or suffering more than 20% of your maximum Health from a single attack., Dual Wield SpecializationDual Wield SpecializationTalentCastInstantIncreases your off-hand weapon damage by 5% and chance to hit with off-hand attacks by 10%. and BloodthirstBloodthirstLevel 40 · Spell · Physical · Rank 1 of 4CastInstantCost300 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown6 sec cooldownDuration10 secInstantly attack the target causing damage equal to 35% of your Attack Power plus 30 and increasing your movement speed by 10% for 10 sec. all still show their pre-October-2 text in game, so Bloodthirst reads 35% of Attack Power rather than 45%. Everything else Forever adds did land: 58 of its 61 new or renamed talents are in, and the three above are the only ones missing.

Three kinds of caveat run through these pages and they do not mean the same thing. Something marked as ours is our own reasoning rather than a source's. Something called a client or a guide-site reading is a number Blizzard has not published. The pass above is a third case: Blizzard has published it and the game does not have it yet.

The hover tooltips on these Warrior pages come from that same build. A few of them print the older number beside prose carrying Blizzard's newer one. Where they disagree, believe the prose: it is Blizzard's figure, and the tooltip is the number the game is still showing.

What Fury is for

Dual-wielding out-generates a two-hander on Rage simply by swinging more often, and it hands you somewhere to dump the surplus: WhirlwindWhirlwindSpell · PhysicalCastInstantCost250 ManaCooldown10 sec cooldownDuration2 secAttacks nearby enemies in a whirlwind of steel that lasts 2 sec. and inflicts normal damage plus 300. now always strikes with both weapons, no talent required, for every Warrior who dual-wields.

The catch is timing. You cannot dual-wield until level 20, and WhirlwindWhirlwindSpell · PhysicalCastInstantCost250 ManaCooldown10 sec cooldownDuration2 secAttacks nearby enemies in a whirlwind of steel that lasts 2 sec. and inflicts normal damage plus 300. is level 36. For the first twenty levels you are a two-handed Warrior with Fury talents, and the spec proper arrives well after that.

No source rates Fury the best Warrior leveller. Icy Veins ties it with Arms at 2.0/5 for Levelling and scores Protection higher at 2.5/5; neither Wowhead nor ClassicWoW.gg publishes a score. What Fury has going for it is that its tier 1 and 2 talents are what every Warrior takes, which is why the published Arms and Fury level-20 builds are identical.

Stat priority

Weapon damage, then Hit, then critical strike, Strength, Agility, Stamina. Hit matters especially while dual-wielding, because a missed swing is rage you never earn. Crit pulls double duty: a critical strike generates 100% increased Rage on top of the crit's extra damage.

The guide sites put Dual Wield SpecializationDual Wield SpecializationTalentCastInstantIncreases your off-hand weapon damage by 5% and chance to hit with off-hand attacks by 10%. at +25% off-hand damage and nothing else. The client disagrees, and reads +5% off-hand damage at full rank for the Warrior talent. Any 50% you see quoted belongs to the Rogue talent of the same name. Blizzard has published no percentage at all, so treat the size of the bonus as unsettled rather than as the +25% three sites print. Off-hand Hit comes from the row 3 talent Furious Precision (+4/7/10%), a separate 3 points rather than riding along with DWS's 5. Furious Precision is not in the game yet (see scope), so there is no off-hand Hit talent you can take right now.

Live bug, not design. Blizzard's own Known Issues list for this build still states that Dual Wield SpecializationDual Wield SpecializationTalentCastInstantIncreases your off-hand weapon damage by 5% and chance to hit with off-hand attacks by 10%. is granting its 2/4/6/8/10% Hit bonus to both your main hand and off-hand, when it should only ever have applied off-hand. A separate line in the same patch notes says the talent was supposed to stop granting off-hand Hit at all. Those two Blizzard statements do not square with each other. What is clear is that the bug gave Blizzard's own testers bad data, which they say is why this whole pass on Fury happened. Do not plan a build around off-hand Hit from this talent until it settles.

Separately, queueing Heroic StrikeHeroic StrikeLevel 1 · Spell · Physical · Rank 1 of 9CastInstantCost150 ManaRangeMeleeA strong attack that increases melee damage by 11 and causes a high amount of threat. no longer raises your off-hand hit chance.

At level 60

Unknown, and Icy Veins is unusually frank about it: "we are unsure currently if there will be additional ways to generate Rage at Level 60, as these changes alone greatly reduce Fury Warrior's Rage generation." That was written against the launch beta, before Blizzard's September 30 post and the October 1–2 builds. Three changes since then land squarely on Fury: the restored crit-Rage bonus (now 100%, see Stat priority), Armor no longer cutting into Rage from damage taken, and Bloodthirst's AP ratio returning to 45%. Some of that shortfall should already be smaller than when Icy Veins wrote it — no source confirms that, it is only the direction the changes point.
